info.title: TorrentMate — the contract the maquette's interface requires
info.description:
WHAT THE NEXT VERSION OF THE FRONTEND NEEDS A SERVER TO ANSWER, declared by the interface rather than read off the backend that exists (D7 of docs/reference/frontend-architecture.md).

IT IS NOT frontend/openapi.json, which is generated FROM the running backend. The two differ on purpose and every difference is a DEMAND, computed by scripts/compare-contracts.py into docs/reference/frontend-backend-demands.md. No backend work happens until the interface is frozen; the register IS the future specification, delivered as a diff rather than a blank page.

SOME FIELDS ARE UGLY ON PURPOSE. Where a maquette fixture holds a pre-formatted string, this contract carries it verbatim rather than decomposing it into facts. That is D-L08-5, and it is what makes the conversion provable: a mock returning exactly what the fixture returns renders the same thing, so the oracle proves the wiring at zero divergence. Every such field says so, and the demand register asks for the underlying fact.

x-seeded-from NAMES THE FIXTURE FAMILIES an operation's mock is seeded from. It is read by scripts/check-mock-seeds.py, so it is a contract and not a note.

x-unseeded IS THE OTHER HALF OF x-seeded-from, and every operation carries exactly one of the two. An operation whose response no fixture covers — an acknowledgement, a count derived from the request, a state token from this contract's own enum — says so in as many words. Without it, « nothing was invented here » and « nobody looked » are the same silence, and scripts/check-mock-seeds.py --arm provenance refuses an operation carrying neither.

get.description: Read when « Supprimer »'s confirmation opens (M2): the torrent still in qBittorrent with its files (`keeps_files`), no torrent or a moved arrival (`only_copy`), or no answer from qBittorrent (`unknown`, treated as the only copy). post.summary: Search a cross-seed for one torrent, on one tracker or on every eligible one
post.description: « Chercher un cross-seed » (OPEN 3 = A, round 9 Q10; demand E): ONE search, asked once, bounded ONLY by the engine's daily quota and its delay between searches — never by the 3-day exclusion window, which governs the automatic sweep alone (F45). The answer is a visible « en file », never « occupé » (DOIT-4, NE-DOIT-PAS-3); a second ask on a pair already searching is the one refusal (409, a duplicate). `tracker` names one pair (the torrent's panel); null asks every eligible pair in the engine's one search (the card's swipe). Its outcome arrives on the stream (`CrossSeedSearched`).

With a tracker, one pair is excluded (a cut does this in its own call).

displayedValue.description: B-090, AND WHAT IS LEFT OF IT. This is the engine's own French summary of the value, rendered for a screen — 59 of the 159 fields differ from `String(raw)`, and two of them LOSE information: a four-element list reads « multi, vf, vostfr +1 » and an eighteen-file list reads « paths.json5, disks.json5, categories.json5 +15 ». NO SURFACE READS IT ANY MORE: the settings panel says the value from `raw` through the interface's own formatter, and `precision` carries the one fact `raw` cannot. It stays declared for one reason — it is what the formatter's test asserts against, 159 strings extracted from `engine/legacy.js@c0a5062ac` and held byte for byte against it while it lived — all 159 of them, `precision` and the `schedule` kind included — which is the only non-vacuous oracle available for a rendering. The engine is gone and the field outlived it: the settings seed (`mocks/seeds/settings.json`) still carries the 159 strings and the formatter's test still holds them, so it dies with that test.

precision.description: how many decimals the value is WRITTEN with, when it has any. JSON holds one number for 4 and 4.0 and the interface shows two different settings — a size in whole gigabytes and a ratio to one decimal — so the schema is the only thing that knows which. Seven fields carry it. B-090: the field this replaces was `displayedValue`, a French summary rendered for a screen, which no control could edit and which had lost the fourth element of a four-element list.

infoHash.description: the torrent the obligation is owed on

sourceTracker.description: the tracker the obligation is owed to

title.description: the title the engine composes for it, or null when it resolves none

dispatchedPath.description: where the dispatch put the files, or null before it did

minimumRatio.description: the ratio floor owed, read from the tracker's economy when the grab happened

minimumSeedTimeSeconds.description: the seed time owed, in seconds

observedRatio.description: the tracker's ratio as last observed, or null when never observed

accumulatedSeedTimeSeconds.description: the seed time accumulated so far, or null when never observed

hitAndRunCount.description: the tracker's hit-and-run count as last observed, or null when never observed

addedAt.description: when the obligation began, Unix-epoch seconds

satisfiedAt.description: when it was met, Unix-epoch seconds, or null

breachedAt.description: when it was broken, Unix-epoch seconds, or null

releasedAt.description: when it ended early — a removal confirmed in the app always sets this — Unix-epoch seconds, or null

crossSeedOf.description: when a cross-seed CREATED the obligation, the torrent it is the copy of; null otherwise

Obligations.description: every seeding obligation the engine holds

Download.description: one qBittorrent ENTRY on one tracker — a torrent cross-seeded onto two trackers is two entries. The backend's `AcquisitionDownload` extended with the tracker it runs on, its ratio there, its deadline and whether it is the origin grab (a demand: none of the four exists)

name.description: the torrent's name in the client

season.description: the season, or null for a movie

episode.description: the episode, or null for a movie or a season pack

state.description: the client's state, in the backend's own tokens

progress.description: how much is downloaded, from 0 to 1

etaSeconds.description: the time left to download, or null when none is running

errorReason.description: why the client refuses it, or null

ids.description: the medium's provider identity — the key its sheet is addressed by — or null when no sheet identifies it

tracker.description: the tracker this entry is active on

origin.description: true for the torrent's origin grab, false for a cross-seed of the same files

ratio.description: the entry's ratio on THIS tracker, computed on the torrent's own size — so a cross-seed never divides by zero

deadline.description: when the obligation on this entry is met by seed time, Unix-epoch seconds, or null when none is owed

addedAt.description: when the client added the entry, Unix-epoch seconds, or null when the client does not say. The backend HAS it on its client item (`TorrentItem.added_on`) and does not route it (a demand, T3)

swarmSeeds.description: how many complete sources the swarm counts, or null when the client does not say — never 0 for an unknown, 0 is a dead swarm. The backend HAS it (`TorrentItem.swarm_seeds`, qBittorrent's `num_complete`) and does not route it (a demand, T3)

swarmLeechers.description: how many incomplete peers the swarm counts, or null when the client does not say. qBittorrent answers `num_incomplete`; the backend does not read it (a demand, T3)

downloadedBytes.description: how much this entry has received, or null when the client does not say. Not read by the backend (a demand, T3)

uploadedBytes.description: how much this entry has sent, or null when the client does not say. Not read by the backend (a demand, T3)

downloadRate.description: the entry's download rate in bytes per second, or null when the client does not say. Not read by the backend (a demand, T3 — a stream demand on `TorrentProgress`)

uploadRate.description: the entry's upload rate in bytes per second, or null when the client does not say. Not read by the backend (a demand, T3 — a stream demand on `TorrentProgress`)

poster.description: the poster of the medium the entry is linked to, or null when it has none or no medium is linked (a demand: the backend's entry carries no artwork)

folder.description: the staging folder the engine holds for this entry — the path to its resolution when no medium is linked — or null when it holds none (a demand)

crossSeed.description: on an ORIGIN entry, its cross-seed tracker by tracker; null on a cross-seed's own entry (its origin's row carries it)

Downloads.description: every entry the download client holds

BrokenObligation.description: an obligation the ENGINE broke whose torrent has already left the client — kept, never lost, until the operator marks it seen

infoHash.description: the torrent it was owed on

title.description: the title the engine composes for it

brokenAt.description: when it was broken, Unix-epoch seconds

seen.description: whether the operator marked it seen; seen is not gone

Tracker.description: one configured tracker as its own subject — nothing in the backend answers a tracker today (a demand)

ratio.description: the account's ratio on this tracker, never averaged with another, or null before anything was downloaded there

downloadedBytes.description: the account's Download volume on this tracker

uploadedBytes.description: the account's Upload volume on this tracker

alertThreshold.description: the ratio under which the tracker is in alert — its own setting, distinct from the floor and the target — or null when none is set

brokenObligations.description: the obligations the engine broke on this tracker, their torrent gone

enabled.description: whether the tracker is switched on — read from the SAME setting the roster's switch and Réglages write, `tracker.providers.<name>.enabled`, so the two agree (a demand: nothing in the backend answers a tracker)

disabled.description: null while the tracker is on; otherwise who switched it off and why. A refused identifier is `reason: identifierRefused` here — one field per fact (a demand, T2: the engine switches nothing off by itself today)

RankingThreshold.description: a size-or-count threshold and the score it awards

at.description: the threshold — bytes for a size, a count for seeders

score.description: the score awarded when the field meets it

RankingCriterion.description: ONE criterion of the acquisition ranking: the field it scores, its weight, and either a score per value (a categorical field) or thresholds (a numeric one)

field.description: the release field it scores — `resolution`, `codec`, `language`, `source`, `provider`, `seeders`, `sizeBytes`, or `trackerRatioState`

weight.description: the multiplier applied to its score

values.description: a score per value, for a categorical field, matched without regard to case

thresholds.description: ordered thresholds, for a numeric field

prefer.description: for thresholds, whether higher or lower is better

RankingBonuses.description: points added for a release's economy

RankingConfig.description: the acquisition ranking: its criteria, the seeders under which a release is excluded, and the bonuses

minSeeders.description: a release with fewer seeders is excluded

RankingSample.description: one release of the preview's FIXED, representative set — the backend's own `_ranking_preview_samples`, as the trackers would parse it

RankingPreviewRelease.description: one sample release scored under the ranking asked for

excluded.description: whether it has fewer seeders than the ranking's `minSeeders` — shown, sunk last, never dropped

trackerRatioState.description: where its tracker's ratio stands against that tracker's own economy — under its floor (`min_ratio`), under its target, or comfortable; null when the tracker has no policy. A DEMAND: `TrackerResult` carries no ratio-derived field (personalscraper/api/tracker/_base.py:58), so no criterion can score it today; `rank()` needs nothing else, a criterion naming this field scores it the way `provider` is scored

RankingPreview.description: the sample set, scored and ordered: the releases kept by score, the excluded ones last

ranked.description: every sample, scored, in the order the ranking puts them

knownTrackers.description: the configured trackers — the values a tracker-keyed criterion is offered

ConfigurationFileContent.description: one configuration file's content, as the file holds it

values.description: its parsed JSON5 content, keyed by its top-level keys

digest.description: the SHA-256 of the file as it lies on disk — what a write compares against

shadowedKeys.description: the keys of this file overridden by `local.json5`

TrackerDisabled.description: why a tracker is off: the operator's own choice, or a failure the engine switched it off for (a demand, T2)

reason.description: the failure's kind, or null when the operator switched it off

message.description: the engine's own sentence for the failure, or null when the operator switched it off

since.description: since when it is off by failure, Unix-epoch seconds, or null when the operator switched it off

DecisionAuthor.description: who settled a decision: the operator, by a pick or a manual search, or the engine, by an identification it made alone. DIVERGENCE: the engine writes no decision row for an identification it made alone — the interface reads one here, as a settled row with `engine` as its author.

owned.description: of those, the ones in the library

queued.description: of those, the ones wanted and not yet held

announced.description: episodes announced and not yet aired

source.description: `unknown` when no aired catalog is cached: the seasons are then empty, never a fabricated all-missing grid

Right.description: ONE RIGHT OF THE ACL (§ 17, ruling 17: every access, a view or an act, is a right). Rights belong to ROLES, never to an account (ruling 20). The interface reads the set an account holds and offers exactly what it opens; it never compares a role's name.

Role.description: A ROLE and the rights it carries (ruling 20: one role per account). Two are the system's and indelible (ruling 22): `admin` holds NO rights list — it bypasses the ACL, every right present and future — and `default` is the role every new account receives, its rights configurable. Every other role is `ordinary` configuration.

name.description: its name, for display only — never compared

kind.description: `admin` and `default` are the two system roles; `ordinary` is everything else

rights.description: the rights it carries — empty for `admin`, which bypasses the list

AccountRef.description: An account named by another answer — a requester, a chooser's row.

AccountSummary.description: ONE ACCOUNT OF THE ROSTER, as « Comptes » and the reassign chooser read it: its name, its mandatory e-mail, its ONE role (ruling 20) and its Plex link.

Roster.description: Every account and every role (demand F).

TrackerCrossSeed.description: one tracker's cross-seed at rest (demand A) — the roster's line, the tracker's panel and the badge read this ONE answer (§ 13). The counts are the engine's, over the SAME pairs the downloads read answers, never recomputed by the interface. invented: no fixture exists for the cross-seed (L17 DESIGN § 2.3)

enabled.description: the tracker's own switch, read from `tracker.providers.<name>.cross_seed` — the setting Réglages and the tracker's panel both write

engineEnabled.description: the engine's own switch, `cross_seed.enabled`; a separate fact from the tracker's (M6) — it cuts nothing running

active.description: how many torrents cross-seed onto this tracker now (pairs in state `active`)

failed.description: how many pairs on this tracker read `error` with a FAILURE-kind reason (the attempt failed, the engine could not finish, the reserved upload slot) — never an ordinary mismatch, never `noMatch` (OPEN 8 = A); a failure leaves the count the moment its pair's state changes (M5)

lastInjectedAt.description: the last injection onto this tracker, Unix-epoch seconds, or null when none ever happened

CrossSeedPair.description: one (torrent, tracker) pair of a cross-seed, read on the ORIGIN entry (demand B): the pair's CURRENT state, the last attempt's own result (§ 13). invented: no fixture exists for the cross-seed (L17 DESIGN § 2.3)

tracker.description: the OTHER tracker the pair names — the engine's `CrossSeedInjected.source_tracker` names this TARGET tracker; the contract says `tracker`

state.description: the pair's state, one of the operator's six words: actif, stoppé (by HISTORY — it ran and was stopped), tracker sans cross-seed (none ever ran and none can), erreur de cross-seed, sans correspondance, pas encore cherché

reason.description: on `error` only: the last attempt's code — the engine's twelve, closed, plus the slot reserved for an upload or tracker-side creation failure (round 8 Q18 = B, no code path emits it today); null otherwise

candidate.description: on `active` and `error`: the candidate's release name on that tracker, or null

waitReason.description: on `notSearched`: why not yet, when the engine knows — the origin still downloading, or waiting for the daily quota; null otherwise

at.description: when the state was taken — the injection on `active`, the attempt on `error` and `noMatch` — Unix-epoch seconds, or null

stoppedAt.description: on `stopped`: when the pair was stopped, Unix-epoch seconds; null otherwise

stopCause.description: on `stopped`: the tracker's switch cut with its « running ones too » option, or the pair cut from the torrent (or its origin removed); null otherwise. The engine's own switch is NEVER a stop cause (M6)

entryHash.description: on `active`: the hash of the cross-seed's own client entry on that tracker, or null

excluded.description: whether the pair is excluded from the engine's future passes (round 9 Q11) — a cut excludes it; an undo lifts it

searching.description: whether a search asked by hand is queued or running for the pair

TorrentCrossSeed.description: an ORIGIN entry's cross-seed (demand B): one pair per OTHER tracker eligible for it. The backend must ATTEMPT every eligible, switched-on tracker — the engine today stops at the first verified injection (DESIGN fact 16) — and must KEEP a state for the pairs no event fires for. invented: no fixture exists for the cross-seed (L17 DESIGN § 2.3)

titleExcluded.description: whether « Ne plus partager ce titre » excluded the whole title from every future pass, on every tracker

CrossSeedQuota.description: the engine's own bounds on a search, shown and never set here (Réglages sets them): the daily quota and the delay between two searches. The 3-day exclusion window governs the automatic sweep only and is never a bound on a hand-provoked search (F45). invented: no fixture exists for the cross-seed (L17 DESIGN § 2.3)

CrossSeedOrigin.description: the torrent a cross-seed's obligation is the copy of (demand D, § 19 point 2). invented: no fixture exists for the cross-seed (L17 DESIGN § 2.3)

media.description: the origin's provider IDs, the path to its sheet (NE-DOIT-PAS-9), or null when unidentified

MediaCrossSeedOrigin.description: one ORIGIN torrent of the medium in the download client, with its cross-seed pairs — the same pairs the downloads read carries on that origin's row (R-L17-b). invented: no fixture exists for the cross-seed (L17 DESIGN § 2.3)

name.description: the torrent's name in the client

tracker.description: the tracker the origin was grabbed on

pairs.description: one per other eligible tracker, in the operator's six words

titleExcluded.description: whether « Ne plus partager ce titre » excluded the whole title

MediaCrossSeed.description: the media sheet's cross-seed block (demand C, § 19: « un bloc par tracker, réservé au profil administrateur »), taken over by L18 from L17 (F25). invented: no fixture exists for the cross-seed (L17 DESIGN § 2.3)

torrents.description: every origin torrent of the medium still in the client; empty when none is

Problem.description: the request failed, and the reason is the real one (NE-DOIT-PAS-4, NE-DOIT-PAS-5)
